rationale.usefulness: The documented connector lets builders compare hosted models in several existing agents, with explicit pinning, configuration prerequisites and usage accounting. The report turns those features into bounded educational-app, website-image and video-preparation trials with acceptance criteria. These are actionable proposals, although neither task quality nor savings has been measured and image support is limited to named surfaces.
rationale.impact: The supported contribution is reducing friction when adopting or comparing hosted models within familiar coding tools. This can matter operationally, but the evidence establishes neither a new model capability nor an independently demonstrated improvement in completed-task cost or quality. Its significance to AI development is therefore modest rather than a substantial methodological advance.
rationale.novelty: Combining existing agent connections, automatic routing, model pinning, usage comparison and selected image workflows is a useful integration. The supplied primary sources do not demonstrate that its mechanisms are technically new or uniquely differentiated against alternatives, so integration convenience warrants only a moderate-low novelty rating.
rationale.maturity: Detailed prerequisites, supported versions, command syntax, desktop-profile behavior and troubleshooting make a limited trial reasonably approachable. Beta status, contradictory session-versus-request routing descriptions and the absence of execution or reliability testing prevent a stronger readiness rating. The report handles these limitations accurately.
rationale.openness: Named hosted models and a documented mechanism for changing models offer some choice and portability of the surrounding workflow. However, requests depend on a hosted gateway and API accounts; the supplied evidence does not establish gateway inspectability or all model licenses and deployment rights. Open-model marketing is correctly kept separate from local inference and comprehensive openness.

concerns: Non-blocking: actual routing frequency, integration fidelity and accepted-task savings remain unverified; the report explicitly discloses these limitations.

Non-blocking editorial opportunity: the saved documentation specifically disables native web search in the ChatGPT Desktop profile. Naming that limitation would make the existing warning about surface-specific integrations more concrete.
